ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Andrea has 4 equally long strips of paper. When she glues two together with an overlap of $10 \mathrm{~cm}$, she gets a strip $50 \mathrm{~cm}$ long. With the other two she wants to make a $56 \mathrm{~cm}$ long strip. How long must the overlap be?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: Image 1 shows two equal paper strips positioned to overlap, and the overlap region is labeled 10 cm. Image 2 shows another pair of equal strips glued with a shaded overlap region marked with a question mark. Reasoning: Let the length of each original strip be L cm. In the first case, gluing two strips with a 10 cm overlap produces a 50 cm strip, so 2L - 10 = 50. Thus 2L = 60 and L = 30 cm. For the second pair, the desired final length is 56 cm. If the unknown overlap is x cm, then 2L - x = 56. Substituting L = 30 gives 60 - x = 56, so x = 4 cm.
